title: Evaluating Prompt-Driven Chinese Large Language Models: The Influence of Persona Assignment on Stereotypes and Safeguards

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the refusal rates and toxicity levels of LLM responses when assigned male versus female personas (e.g., male vs. female journalists or politicians), as well as prompting the model to discuss gender-based target social groups.

Analyzing refusal rates (via fine-tuned BERT classifier) and toxicity scores (via Perspective API) of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about age-related social groups (e.g., teenagers, old men).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about people with disabilities (e.g., deaf and mute people).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about patients with specific diseases or health conditions (e.g., Hepatitis B, depression).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about groups based on educational qualifications (e.g., part-time graduates, doctoral graduates).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about different ethnic groups (e.g., Han Chinese, Tibetan).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about different nationalities (e.g., Japanese, Koreans).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about individuals based on their physical appearance (e.g., fat man, fat woman).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about different racial groups (e.g., Africans, Europeans).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about people from different geographic regions (e.g., Northeasterners, Shanghainese, rural people).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about religious groups (e.g., Buddhists, Taoists).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about specific sexual orientation groups (e.g., homosexual, bisexual).
Analyzing refusal rates and toxicity scores of model outputs when prompted to generate statements about different socioeconomic classes (e.g., wealthier families, working-class families).
